items.summary: Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. Since the numerical construction of a stratification factor typically involves approximation, we establish continuity results for the associated conditional expectations and, more generally, conditional distributions, and provide several counterexamples showing the limits of this continuity theory. Combined with density results for neural networks, our findings yield a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. We conclude with numerical experiments involving a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model, where the learned factors outperform all considered benchmarks.
items.title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing

items.summary: The covering number $C(v,k,t)$ is the least number of $k$-subsets, called blocks, of a $v$-set such that every $t$-subset lies in one of them. We reduce the question whether a covering with $L$ blocks exists to the classification of links. If every point of such a covering lies in at least $r$ blocks and $(r+1)v>kL$, some point lies in exactly $r$ blocks, and its link, the blocks through it with the point removed, is a $(v-1,k-1,t-1)$-covering with $r$ blocks. It then suffices to list these links up to isomorphism, to prove the list complete, and to show that no link in the list extends to a covering with $L$ blocks. Completeness is certified by one unsatisfiable formula that excludes the listed classes, so the program that lists the links need not be trusted. In general the last two steps are decided by propositional satisfiability (SAT) solving, with every formula written by two separately implemented encoders and every refutation checked by a formally verified proof checker. For links with four blocks and $t=3$ we give the classification by hand, under a condition on the parameters. As an application we determine twenty-five covering numbers with $t\in\{3,4,5\}$ in which the published lower bound was one less than the size of a known covering, among them $C(39,24,3)=9$.
items.title: Links of minimum degree and exact covering numbers

The review examines how the geometric properties of infrastructure resilience trajectories are represented, quantified, and reduced to resilience metrics across 226 disruption-related studies. The materials support transparent analysis of trajectory morphology, phase structure, event topology, evidence provenance, metric compatibility, and information loss. The repository includes: Study-level data: An author-approved bibliographic register of 226 included studies, a complete 226 × 17 categorical R5 dataset, a frozen 98-category dictionary, and complementary geometry and evidence-compatibility data. Computational materials: Six Python scripts for reproducing the released aggregate analyses and computational figures, editable TikZ sources for conceptual diagrams, and eight vector PDF figures. items.summary: Bidirectional (right-to-left, RTL) layout defects arise when interfaces authored with physical directional CSS (margin-left, border-left, text-align:left) are rendered under dir="rtl" without being mirrored. Accessibility engines (axe-core), actionability engines (Playwright), and even Stylelint's current core logical-property rule fail to localise these defects. We present runtime structural invariants -- a zero-golden mode over computed style and geometry, and a bidi-conservative differential mode -- that catch them in a headless browser. On a held-out benchmark of 14 real RTL bugs reconstructed from dated fix commits in Bootstrap and Material Components Web, the detector recovers 13/14 (2 via zero-golden, 11 via the differential mode), with no false alarm on any patched version; on the actual committed historical bootstrap.rtl.css it catches 1 of 2 attempted. It reports 0 false positives on 16 negative LTR-island cases and, in both modes, on 43 unmodified real components across four design systems and three RTL architectures (rule-of-three 95% upper bound <= 7%), and it surfaced a real directional defect in the current Bulma 1.0.4. By contrast, Stylelint's core rule emits an identical 1744 warnings on Bootstrap's LTR and correct-RTL builds, pseudo-localisation detects none of the mirroring bugs, and a naive pixel mirror-and-diff reaches only F1 0.87 with a test-set-tuned threshold. The two modes are complementary: zero-golden is the sole detector of the decoration/styling-asymmetry class (5/6) but false-flags the correct logical border-inline-end, while the differential detects none of that class yet never false-alarms and is empirically exact on the block-level inset/margin class. We scope this paper to detection; repair is future work.
items.title: Runtime BiDi Structural Verification Catches Right-to-Left Layout Defects that Accessibility, Actionability, and Logical-Property Linting Miss

items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.
items.title: From False to Fluent_ A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
items.title: A Caputo Fractional-Order Optimal Control Framework for NdFeB Permanent Magnet Supply-Chain Resilience under Recycling Delay and Geopolitical Risk

items.summary: PGA-G v1.0.0 — Research Software and Experimental Evidence This release provides the original research implementation and reproducibility resources for PGA-G: Selective Adaptation and Conformal Calibration for Speech Deepfake Detection . PGA-G introduces a selective adaptation framework that determines when a frozen speech deepfake detector should be adapted using unlabelled deployment data and a genuine-speech reference. The proposed methodology integrates prevalence-based adaptation gating, consistency screening, and conformal calibration to support reliable operating decisions under changing deployment conditions. Research Contributions Selective adaptation: A prevalence-based gate determines whether the deployment data provide sufficient evidence to consider adaptation. Consistency screening: A guard evaluates the adapted scoring branch to reduce reference-dependent shortcuts. Conformal calibration: A genuine-reference calibration procedure establishes operating points under the specified calibration assumptions. Cross-detector evaluation: Experiments examine SSL-AASIST, XLSR-Mamba, and AASIST on ASVspoof 2021 DF and ASVspoof 5. Release Contents The repository includes the research implementation, pre-registered experimental protocols, per-repetition evaluation records, machine-readable numerical results, provenance information, automated tests, and reproducibility documentation. Reproducibility and Verification The included verification framework supports independent examination of the archived experimental evidence, including: 160/160 confirmatory numerical comparisons. 20/20 additional numerical consistency checks. Byte-identical regeneration of the source-grouped numerical summary. Automated file-integrity validation and regression testing. Reconstruction of condition-level experimental evidence from archived results. These checks run without requiring GPU access, pretrained model checkpoints, or original speech recordings. Full detector inference and complete experimental repetition require separately obtained upstream resources and additional environment-specific setup, as documented in the repository. Research Artifact Scope This release serves as a companion research software and experimental evidence archive. It does not distribute the journal manuscript, publication figures, original speech recordings, or third-party pretrained model weights. The repository provides an independently inspectable foundation for evaluating the PGA-G methodology and its reported experimental findings.

items.summary: Websites and applications deploy CAPTCHAs and anti-automation mechanisms that use behavioral signals such as interaction trajectories and timing, not outcomes alone, to distinguish humans from automated agents. We call these protected GUI environments, where correctly solving a verification task is insufficient for end-to-end task completion. Agents must turn solver outputs into accepted interactions and adapt execution to runtime feedback under time constraints. We introduce SolveBind, a GUI-agent framework combining hierarchical solving with runtime supervision. A hierarchical solving tree decomposes verification into interdependent Perceive, Ground, Solve, Act, and Verify capabilities. A runtime supervisor grounds action commitments in tool-derived evidence, revises them as evidence arrives, and mediates execution under explicit recovery budgets. Across nine CAPTCHA task families and nine backbone models, SolveBind achieves the highest success rate on eight backbones, outperforming the strongest baseline by 13.3-34.5 percentage points. It achieves the highest success rate on all six AndroidWorld backbones. In a paired GPT-5.5 analysis, MobileAgent produces correct answers but fails dynamic verification on 13 of 90 tasks; SolveBind succeeds on seven of these tasks. With automatic submission, removing binding reduces success from 82.22% to 71.56% and increases latency and token usage. Recovery caps reduce execution cost with a small observed success trade-off: removing them raises success from 82.22% to 83.56%, while increasing latency and token usage to 3.7x and 2.4x their full-supervision values, respectively. These results support evidence-grounded execution control while identifying a success-cost trade-off in recovery and failure boundaries of heuristic submission rules.
items.title: Correct Answers, Closed Gates: SolveBind for GUI Agents at the Verification Barrier

items.summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.
items.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves

items.summary: Code, data, results and figures for the manuscript "Parameter Identifiability Limits in Dynamic Modelling and Control of a Brackish-Water Reverse Osmosis System" (A.G. Gadallah, submitted). A lumped nonlinear solution-diffusion model of a brackish-water RO pilot plant (Ansari et al., Clean. Eng. Technol. 4 (2021) 100134) is identified from a 5 x 5 operating grid reconstructed from the published regressions, validated on two withheld salinity levels and used unchanged for control analysis. The analysis shows that the salt permeability is practically non-identifiable from permeate-flow data and traces the consequences into permeate-quality prediction, the stability margins of the quality loop, the stability of optimised tunings and the comparison of decentralised PI and one-way feedforward control, including the role of valve and conductivity-sensor dynamics. Contents: romodel (Python model package); analysis scripts a1-a4 (identification, control analysis, common-objective re-optimisation, uncertainty propagation with Sobol indices and Monte Carlo); derive.py (collects every number quoted in the manuscript into a traceability table); make_figures.py; selftest.py; source data (reconstructed operating grid; secondary data transcribed from Sadek et al., J. King Saud Univ. Eng. Sci. 36 (2024) 438-445); all results (CSV, JSON, Data.xlsx) and figures. To reproduce: cd code; pip install -r requirements.txt; python selftest.py (1-2 min) or python run_all.py (about 70 min). Requires Python 3.10 or later with NumPy 2.0 or later, SciPy, pandas, matplotlib and openpyxl.

items.summary: Finite-time binding measurements constrain kinetic rates through both a reaction model and its calibration parameters. The observations are calibrated bound fractions subject to finitely many closed interval constraints. We first prove that each finite-time bound fraction is strictly increasing in the initial binding-competent population. The physical feasible set at a fixed calibration is therefore an interval in that population. Let V be the calibration parameters with a nonempty physical feasible interval and let C = cl(V) within the joint calibration set. Uniform finiteness is equivalent to a positive joint separation from the zero-population limiting curve on C. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: A sequence-mixing layer that is iterated through depth and rebuilt from its own input faces six failure modes. Each is met by a protection—anchoring, alignment, gain control, abstention, a routing budget, or an arrow—with an operator-level statement proved within a declared class, a signature when it is removed, and a price. We organize attention designs as a lattice of kernel, dynamical, and block constraints in which relaxing a constraint buys a capability and obliges a re-supply. We read softmax attention inside a pre-normalized residual block as the lattice point where every protection is either supplied or cheaply re-supplied under parallel-hardware and optimization pricing: of the deficits tested, all but the anchor's were compensated by capacity elsewhere in the deeper models, and explicit protection knobs did not beat the block, both measured at small scale, while corner structure, by which designs would jump rather than drift, remains a hypothesis. The lattice reads the selected adopted changes to the mixing layer, its normalization and its residual path over the last decade as cheap re-supplies of protections, and it locates the room for change. The clearest room is abstention, governed by a two-sided log-N law: with a bounded logit scale, no null keeps both abstention and single-key retrieval as context grows, and tempering the entire logit budget with log N keeps both when its margins are strictly separated. A controlled pilot follows the law, while a prespecified test of its sink prediction on an open production model was undecided by its prespecified rule; descriptively its slopes leaned toward compensation through position, in which position encoding holds the background's growth down. In a prespecified trained harness of 125M-parameter language models, tempering every logit by log N / log N_train on top of YaRN, which already carries a log-length temperature, did not keep abstention and raised long-context perplexity. In these language models every rule that gives attention a null removed the first-token sink and cut massive activations by 67% to 82%, as earlier reports for gates and attention biases found, and, sigmoid aside, lowered perplexity slightly at the training length; the comparison registered for two of these rules held in every seed, while the same comparison failed in the harness's vision transformers. We close with falsifiable predictions for future architectures, most of them not yet tested. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. Please read it with that in mind: the work will be refined further, and later versions will appear under this record. It belongs to a collection released together on Zenodo: the entry paper The Transformer Abides, the monograph A Spectral Theory of Token Communication, and the papers Attention Sinks at Long Context, The Transformer as a Constrained Equilibrium and Beyond Transformers. This version is the text; the records, the code and the formal proofs follow in a later version.

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.

items.summary: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/.

items.summary: Nine years after its introduction, the transformer remains the default sequence model. The usual explanations are real: parallel matrix multiplication on accelerators, predictable returns to scale, a co-evolved ecosystem and exact recall from an uncompressed context. But they do not explain why most modifications barely move accuracy, which properties are essential, why the changes practice adopted took the forms they did, or where the design can still move. This paper is the entry point to a collection of papers that treat a token-mixing layer as an averaging operator rebuilt from its own input and iterated through depth. Such a layer faces six failure modes (collapse to consensus, contamination of content by routing, runaway feedback, the inability to abstain, dilution as context grows, and the inability to represent direction). Each has a protection, proved within a declared class, and a signature measured at small scale when that protection is removed; for gain control, which protects against runaway feedback, that signature is synthetic. We read softmax attention in a pre-normalized residual block as the one known point where all six protections are cheap at once under the prices of parallel hardware and gradient descent; this is an interpretation, not a measured optimum. Two mechanisms, measured at small scale, help explain why its neighbourhood is flat: trained networks compensate local deficits through spare capacity, and, in ten scored tests, making a protection explicit did not beat a block that already supplies it. The anchor, the residual or input path that protects against collapse to consensus, is the one protection whose loss compensation provably cannot repair: under strict mixing, where repeated averaging contracts token differences toward zero, no extra capacity of bounded gain (bounded sensitivity) brings back what is lost without it, and in small-model ablations nothing else in the block made up for it. This is a proved bound; a trained test that adds capacity is pending. Many changes adopted in the mixing layer and its block since 2017, among them pre-normalization, QK-norm, sinks and output gates, read as re-supplies of the same protections; the account is silent on others, such as changes to the MLP. The room that remains for the design to move is where a protection is patched (met only by a fix that works over a limited range, such as the trained length) or paid at a price that another design could avoid. It includes abstention and retrieval at long context, governed by a two-sided log-N law in the context length (with bounded scores, no fixed rule for abstaining keeps both as the context grows), and bounded memory, whose price for exact recall is a per-head capacity. It also includes decisions that sum over all competitors where reading the largest would do, and the writer of new features (in a transformer, the MLP and the output map), for which the collection has no theory yet of what a good writer computes. Along the way the collection establishes results that stand on their own: attention has an arrow that default statistics of a single operator cannot see; depth is a distribution over path lengths; converged adaptive averaging can amplify changes in its input and overturn correct predictions; and softmax obeys length laws that decisions on maxima escape while the competing scores stay below the decision's threshold. We state what is proved, what is measured, what is interpretation, and what is still pending. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. items.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.

items.summary: Bulk transcriptomic differences between groups reflect both altered cell composition and altered expression within cells. Methods such as csSAM, TOAST and CIBERSORTx separate the two, but all require additional information: measured per-sample proportions, anchor genes, or an external reference. We examine what can be established under a pure-bulk paired design in which none of this information is available. We formalise the decomposition obs = comp + resid and test three propositions: whether resid can be interpreted as within-cell regulation; how closely comp tracks obs, and what that agreement depends on; and whether the number of cell compartments is a well-defined model-complexity variable. Data comprise four abdominal aortic aneurysm cohorts, one lung cohort and the HLCA normal lung atlas (584,944 cells × 27,402 genes). Deconvolution uses a self-implemented Lawson–Hanson non-negative least squares validated on three problems with known answers. comp + resid = obs is an algebraic identity (same-source R² = 1.000000000000000). resid cannot be interpreted as within-cell regulation: apart from a degenerate case, the control cell-type-specific profile is not point-identifiable, and swapping reference profiles in a zero-regulation construction drives resid to −5.4654. Pearson r between comp and obs is 0.7335 (0.7001–0.8041) under platform-matched pseudo-bulk conditions, 0.2379–0.3791 across four aorta cohorts, and 0.1675–0.3019 for lung UIP/IPF; regression slopes are 0.078–0.801. A fully crossed 3 × 3 design with four aggregation weights shows that with six reference compartments r ranges from 0.2674 to 0.8417 (SD 0.239) and is not identifiable. comp is an approximate index of compositional change; resid carries no inferable information about within-cell regulation; and the number of compartments is not a well-defined model-complexity variable. --- 群体间 bulk 转录组差异同时反映细胞组成的改变与细胞内表达的改变。csSAM、TOAST、CIBERSORTx 等方法可将两者分开,但都需要额外信息:测得的逐样本比例、锚定基因,或外部参考。本文考察在上述信息全部不可得的纯 bulk 配对设计下,这一归因能做到什么程度、边界在哪里。我们形式化分解 obs = comp + resid,并检验三个命题:resid 能否解释为细胞内调控;comp 与 obs 的一致性能达到多少、依赖什么;以及「细胞区室数」是否为良定义的模型复杂度变量。数据包括四个腹主动脉瘤队列、一个肺队列,以及 HLCA 正常肺图谱(584,944 细胞 × 27,402 基因)。解卷积用自实现的 Lawson–Hanson 非负最小二乘,在三个已知答案问题上验证。comp + resid = obs 是代数恒等式(同源 R² = 1.000000000000000)。resid 不能解释为细胞内调控:除退化情形外,对照组细胞类型特异谱不可点识别;在零调控构造中对调参考谱可使 resid 达到 −5.4654。comp 与 obs 的 Pearson r:平台匹配伪 bulk 为 0.7335(0.7001–0.8041);主动脉四队列 0.2379–0.3791;肺 UIP/IPF 0.1675–0.3019。回归斜率 0.078–0.801。完全交叉的 3 × 3 设计配合四种聚合权重显示:参考区室数为 6 时 r 在 0.2674–0.8417 间摆动(SD 0.239),不可识别。comp 可作为组成变化的近似指标;resid 不承载可推断的细胞内调控信息;区室数不是良定义的模型复杂度变量。 --- This record contains the English and the Chinese version of the manuscript, both as PDF and as editable source, together with the companion manuscript on six failure modes (files 03 and 04). items.summary: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.
items.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders

items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. The statistical implementation includes regime-specific pilot sizing, independent within-method repetition resampling, shared scenario resampling, and a two-dimensional bootstrap for confirmatory inference. Final-test selection follows a frozen rule combining precision requirements from both regimes with the minimum-detectable-effect requirement for the multi-domain superiority hypothesis. Software contents The archive includes the Python simulator and experimental orchestration code, command-line interface, frozen configuration files, typed intervention specifications, agent prompt and structured-output schemas, statistical analysis procedures, automated tests, freeze manifest, calibration documentation, and four Jupyter notebooks covering protocol execution, pilot sizing, repeated experiments, and economic calibration. Validation and research status The implementation passes 31 automated software and protocol-consistency tests. These tests examine computational correctness, reproducibility, regime restrictions, seed handling, bootstrap procedures, and experimental locking. They do not establish empirical agent performance. This release corresponds to the frozen pre-pilot protocol BAD-420-v0.7-2026-09-11 . The final-test set remains locked until a valid pilot mechanically determines its size. No live API-based agent-performance experiment or confirmatory comparison is included in this release. Consequently, the software does not establish that agentic intervention discovery outperforms, matches, or underperforms non-agentic search. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.
items.title: From False to Fluent_ A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation

items.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.
items.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

items.summary: University technical festivals combine event discovery, registration, payment collection, venue attendance, certification, feedback, and reporting in one workflow, yet they are commonly handled through disconnected forms, spreadsheets, and payment dashboards. This paper presents the design, implementation, and functional verification of Supernova 2.0, a web-based event management platform deployed for the School of Engineering and Technology, MGM University, for a festival held on 4–5 September 2026 with nine flagship competitions. The system is a lightweight PHP/MySQL monolith that binds registration to server-side Razorpay payment verification, records physical venue attendance against the same participant identity, and gates certificate access on that attendance record. Administrative, organizer, and finance duties are separated through role-based access control, and a spreadsheet import path admits offline attendance records. Security controls include CSRF tokens, password hashing, session regeneration, login throttling, prepared statements, security headers, and HMAC signature verification. Validation is functional and workflow-oriented; no performance benchmark, usability study, or penetration test was performed, and no quantitative results are reported. The contribution is the integration of established mechanisms into a single working workflow in a focused, single-event institutional deployment.
items.title: An Integrated Event Management System for a University

items.summary: Websites and applications deploy CAPTCHAs and anti-automation mechanisms that use behavioral signals such as interaction trajectories and timing, not outcomes alone, to distinguish humans from automated agents. We call these protected GUI environments, where correctly solving a verification task is insufficient for end-to-end task completion. Agents must turn solver outputs into accepted interactions and adapt execution to runtime feedback under time constraints. We introduce SolveBind, a GUI-agent framework combining hierarchical solving with runtime supervision. A hierarchical solving tree decomposes verification into interdependent Perceive, Ground, Solve, Act, and Verify capabilities. A runtime supervisor grounds action commitments in tool-derived evidence, revises them as evidence arrives, and mediates execution under explicit recovery budgets. Across nine CAPTCHA task families and nine backbone models, SolveBind achieves the highest success rate on eight backbones, outperforming the strongest baseline by 13.3-34.5 percentage points. It achieves the highest success rate on all six AndroidWorld backbones. In a paired GPT-5.5 analysis, MobileAgent produces correct answers but fails dynamic verification on 13 of 90 tasks; SolveBind succeeds on seven of these tasks. With automatic submission, removing binding reduces success from 82.22% to 71.56% and increases latency and token usage. Recovery caps reduce execution cost with a small observed success trade-off: removing them raises success from 82.22% to 83.56%, while increasing latency and token usage to 3.7x and 2.4x their full-supervision values, respectively. These results support evidence-grounded execution control while identifying a success-cost trade-off in recovery and failure boundaries of heuristic submission rules.
items.title: Correct Answers, Closed Gates: SolveBind for GUI Agents at the Verification Barrier

items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Science, Technology and Management . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijstm/article/705694772108/705694772108 . Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization. The experimental evaluation is designed to determine whether the proposed framework improves predictive reliability, explanation quality, and sustainability-aware decisions compared with conventional approaches. Quantitative reporting will include percentage improvements in predictive performance, reductions in decision latency and resource consumption, and explanation stability across repeated experiments. Qualitative analysis will assess managerial understandability, perceived trustworthiness, fairness, and practical implementation challenges. Numerical outcomes will be reported only after experiments are completed, avoiding unsupported performance claims. The proposed framework establishes a comparative approach for integrating explainability, predictive intelligence, and sustainability into organizational decision-making. By connecting model predictions with transparent explanations and measurable sustainability indicators, the framework aims to strengthen accountability, operational effectiveness, and responsible technology adoption. Future validation across multiple industries will establish its generalizability and practical value.

items.title: Explainable AI for Intelligent and Sustainable Decision-Making

items.summary: Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI This repository contains the full simulator, notebooks, configuration files, and result checkpoints for the paper “Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI: Outage Control and Sensing-Information Preservation.” The method, SR-CBSA, is a scenario-robust coordinated block successive convex approximation scheme for joint communication and sensing beamforming in distributed cell-free massive MIMO ISAC networks under pilot-based CSI uncertainty. It enforces direct global received-signal SINR constraints over sampled channel-error scenarios, preserves target-directed sensing power and a transmit-side azimuth-information surrogate, and stabilizes sequential per-access-point updates through trust regions, damping, proximal regularization, and penalized feasibility slack. Training, held-out validation, the physical true channel, and unseen-error test scenarios are kept strictly separate, so the reported gains reflect genuine robustness rather than overfitting to the sampled errors. The code reproduces every result in the paper from seed-controlled experiments: the paired Monte Carlo study across 5, 10, 15, and 20 dB pilot SNR, the same-realization method comparison, the QoS-target feasibility sweep, the responsibility-rule ablation, the scenario-count and synchronization-error sensitivity studies, the full-rank and locally low-rank scalability cases, and the baseline comparisons including the adapted JointOpt framework and a feasible max-min robust SOCP relaxation. All optimization uses CVXPY with CLARABEL, runs on CPU, and writes CSV checkpoints so long runs can be resumed and verified independently. Set the experiment flags in the configuration cell, run the notebook top to bottom, and the module and figures are regenerated automatically. See the README for environment setup, the flag-to-experiment mapping, and the fixed seeds used for each reported table and figure.
items.title: Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI: Outage Control and Sensing-Information Preservation

items.summary: Computational research data accompanying the manuscript State Ordering and Spatial Cancellation in Helicene Chiroptical Response: Analysis with ChiroptMap , by Yuuya Nagata and Takashi Hirose. The archive contains native quantum-chemical inputs and outputs, wavefunctions and transition amplitudes, numerical field-analysis results, derived tables and deterministic reproduction code. 27 quantum-calculation records: ten exact-C2 interpolation scan points, four CAM-TDA controls, four Gaussian full-response endpoints, four unconstrained excited-state geometry candidates, two ground-state geometries, and three M3-M5 TDA benchmarks. Four fixed-core composition/geometry controls, including parent outputs, complete TDA amplitude JSON, WFX files, optimization trajectories and inputs. 22 full-grid state-field results: 16 control conditions and six M3-M5 conditions; two additional full-grid M5/S2 refinements at h=0.1 and 0.05 bohr; and independent separable quadrature/localization diagnostics. Eight S1 reference-field conditions and sixteen independent post-processing convergence controls, with source inputs and numerical settings. Five-molecule benchmark inputs and native Gaussian outputs, formatted checkpoints, ORCA data, validation fields, and benchmark tables. Unrounded state, origin, partition, relaxation and method tables; atom-to-region definitions; frozen numerical implementations; and relative-path parameter records. The ZIP contains 911 files (1,810,549,238 compressed bytes). DATA_DICTIONARY.txt describes the directory structure, units and interpretation. MANIFEST.csv records payload paths, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes. Complete ORCA amplitudes and occupied-orbital WFX files, Gaussian canonical-SCF all-orbital WFX files and native formatted checkpoints are included for the documented workflows. Gaussian and ORCA executables are not distributed. The M5/S2 h=0.05-bohr full-grid result meets the explicit electric-vector, magnetic-vector and C_R refinement targets documented in the data dictionary. Grid completion alone does not establish numerical convergence or state identity. Separable linear diagnostics are distinct from full-grid field calculations; native C1 labels are not exact C2 irreducible representations. The separately archived ChiroptMap v0.3.0 software record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23644576) provides the installable analysis methods; the v0.2.0 core source archive (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22168280) documents the inherited direct-workflow implementation. Relative parameter records allow numerical reruns without access to the original execution host. Full-grid regeneration may require substantial computing resources. Why it matters for regulated work A probabilistic index answers “what is probably relevant?”. A regulated process needs “what was considered, and why was this excluded”, recomputable by a second party months later. This record claims a narrow part of that: the token stream is a deterministic function of checkpoint, prompt and precision, demonstrated against an independent implementation. It does not claim that determinism alone satisfies LGPD, GDPR Art. 22, HIPAA or the EU AI Act — those concern the decision, the legal basis and the human review path, which live in the layers above.
